PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Jesus teaches forgiveness in Matthew 5:39. If someone slaps you on the right cheek, you are not to strike back. In this sub-strand you will learn why forgiving matters, how to resist vengeance, and how to refuse to repay evil with evil.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.6: Forgiveness
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) outline the importance of forgiving others
b) resist vengeance as outlined in Mathew 5:39
c) appreciate forgiveness by not repaying evil for evil

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you not pay evil for evil?

## Values
• Love: is portrayed as learners sing a song about loving others.
• Peace: is nurtured as learners say why they should not revenge when wronged.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion: learners sing a song about loving others.
• Peace Education: learners practise reconciliation by forgiving others when wronged.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read and learn new words.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners role play and sing.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.6 Forgiveness
• Matthew 5:39

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Why we forgive

LESSON 1: WHY WE FORGIVE
========================

## What you will learn
• Outline the importance of forgiving others.
• Explain Matthew 5:39 and resist vengeance.

Curriculum outcomes: a) outline the importance of forgiving others; b) resist vengeance as outlined in Mathew 5:39

## Introduction
A slap hurts. The first wish is often to slap back. Jesus gives a different command in Matthew 5:39. Forgiveness refuses to take revenge.

## Notes
Matthew 5:39 says: do not resist an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other cheek also. The design spells the Gospel "Mathew" in one place and "Matthew" in another. The verse is the same. Read it, write it, and recite it.

### What the verse means
A slap on the cheek is an insult as well as a pain. Turning the other cheek means you do not pay the insult back with another insult or another blow. Vengeance is paying back harm for harm. Jesus tells His followers to resist that wish.

The verse does not tell you to stay in a dangerous secret. If someone is beating you, abusing you, or threatening you, you still tell a parent, a teacher or the police. Refusing revenge is not the same as hiding harm. You can report the harm and still refuse to strike back.

### Why forgiveness is important
- Jesus commands it.
- Revenge multiplies fights. Forgiveness stops the chain.
- Forgiveness keeps peace in the class and at home.
- It frees your own heart from staying angry, which Ephesians 4:26 also warns against.
- It shows love for the person who wronged you.
- God forgives people who repent. We are to forgive others.

### Resisting vengeance
When you are wronged, pause. Do not lift your hand. Do not plan a later attack. Say, "I will not pay back evil." Pray. If you need justice, tell a responsible adult and let that adult handle the matter. Role-play a push in the corridor: one learner is pushed, and instead of pushing back says, "Stop. I forgive you," and walks away to tell the teacher if the pushing continues.

Write Matthew 5:39, display it in class, and recite it until it comes to mind before your fist does.

## Key words
• forgiveness — letting go of the wish to punish someone who wronged you
• vengeance — paying back harm with harm
• resist — to refuse to give in

## Activity: Read Matthew 5:39 and role-play
You will need: Bible, Manila paper, Marker
1. Read Matthew 5:39 and say why it is important to forgive others.
2. Write the verse on manila paper, display it in class, and recite it.
3. Role-play acts of forgiveness, such as forgiving a classmate who took a pencil or bumped you.
4. Say why you should not take revenge when you are wronged.

## Practice
1. What does Matthew 5:39 say about a slap on the right cheek?
2. What is vengeance?
3. Give two reasons why forgiveness is important.
4. If someone is abusing you, does forgiveness mean you keep it secret?

## Summary
• Matthew 5:39 teaches us not to strike back.
• Vengeance pays harm with harm. Jesus says to resist it.
• Forgiveness brings peace, and serious harm must still be reported.

### Answers to practice
1. Do not strike back. Turn the other cheek also.
2. Paying back harm with harm.
3. Any two: Jesus commands it; it stops fights; it brings peace; it frees the heart; it shows love; God forgives, so we forgive.
4. No. Tell a trusted adult. Forgiveness refuses revenge. It does not hide harm.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Do not repay evil for evil

LESSON 2: DO NOT REPAY EVIL FOR EVIL
====================================

## What you will learn
• Explain what it means not to repay evil for evil.
• Choose a peaceful response when wronged.

Curriculum outcomes: c) appreciate forgiveness by not repaying evil for evil

## Introduction
Evil repaid with evil makes two wrongs. Jesus' followers appreciate forgiveness by choosing a different path. They do not answer an unkind act with another unkind act.

## Notes
To repay evil for evil means to answer a wrong with a matching wrong. Someone insults you, so you insult them. Someone hides your book, so you hide theirs. Someone gossips, so you spread a worse story. Matthew 5:39 rules this out. Appreciating forgiveness means you value it enough to practise it.

### Peaceful responses
- Speak calmly: "Please stop."
- Move away from the quarrel.
- Forgive in your heart and, when it is safe, say so.
- Pray for the person.
- Tell a teacher if the wrong continues or if you are hurt.
- Sing about loving others so that love, not revenge, stays in your mouth.

Peace grows where learners practise reconciliation. Reconciliation means becoming friends again after a wrong. It needs an apology and forgiveness. If the other person is not ready, you can still refuse to repay evil. You do not have to wait for a perfect apology before you drop the plan for revenge.

### What forgiveness is not
It is not saying that wrong is right. The slap was still wrong. It is not letting a bully rule the class. Tell the teacher. It is not a feeling that arrives before you decide. You may still feel hurt and choose not to strike back.

Love is the value underneath this lesson. A song about loving others helps the class remember that the person who wronged you is still a person God made. Treat that person with peace, and let God and the rightful adults deal with justice.

## Key words
• repay — to give back something in return
• reconciliation — becoming friends again after a wrong
• peace — living without fighting or revenge

## Activity: A song and a peaceful reply
You will need: The displayed copy of Matthew 5:39
1. Recite Matthew 5:39 from the display in class.
2. In pairs, practise a peaceful reply to an insult, without paying it back.
3. Say why you should not repay evil for evil.
4. Sing a song about loving others.

## Practice
1. What does it mean to repay evil for evil?
2. Give one peaceful response when a classmate insults you.
3. Does forgiving mean the wrong action was acceptable?

## Summary
• Do not answer a wrong with another wrong.
• Choose calm words, prayer and, when needed, a report to a teacher.
• Forgiveness values peace more than revenge.

### Answers to practice
1. To answer a wrong action with another wrong action.
2. Any one: speak calmly, move away, forgive, pray, or tell a teacher if it continues.
3. No. The wrong is still wrong. Forgiveness refuses to pay it back with another wrong.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 3.6 FORGIVENESS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Matthew 5:39 teaches that if someone slaps your right cheek you should:
   A. slap them harder
   B. turn the other cheek and not strike back
   C. plan revenge for later
   D. hide the verse

2. Vengeance means...
   A. paying back harm with harm
   B. forgiving at once
   C. praying for an enemy
   D. telling the truth

3. Why is forgiveness important?

4. Resisting vengeance means...
   A. giving in to the wish to hit back
   B. refusing to take revenge
   C. insulting louder
   D. hiding every wrong forever, including abuse

5. If a person is abusing you, forgiveness means you:
   A. keep it a secret
   B. strike back first
   C. tell a trusted adult and still refuse revenge
   D. repay them in secret

6. Repaying evil for evil means...
   A. answering a wrong with another wrong
   B. forgiving
   C. sharing lunch
   D. reciting a verse

7. A classmate hides your book. A peaceful response is:
   A. hiding their book
   B. telling them calmly to return it, and telling the teacher if needed
   C. spreading a lie about them
   D. slapping them

8. Forgiveness does not mean...
   A. the wrong was acceptable
   B. you stop wanting revenge
   C. you can pray for the person
   D. peace is better than a fight

9. Which value grows when you sing about loving others and refuse revenge?
   A. Love and peace
   B. Pride and revenge
   C. Fear and gossip
   D. Greed

10. Reconciliation means...
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 3.6 FORGIVENESS
========================================

1. B. turn the other cheek and not strike back
   The verse says not to resist an evil person by striking back.

2. A. paying back harm with harm
   Vengeance is revenge.

3. Any one: Jesus commands it; it stops fights from growing; it brings peace; it shows love.
   Forgiveness protects peace and obeys Jesus.

4. B. refusing to take revenge
   To resist vengeance is to refuse revenge. Serious harm is still reported.

5. C. tell a trusted adult and still refuse revenge
   Reporting harm and refusing revenge belong together.

6. A. answering a wrong with another wrong
   That pattern is what Jesus' teaching rules out.

7. B. telling them calmly to return it, and telling the teacher if needed
   You do not repay the wrong. You seek a peaceful and truthful solution.

8. A. the wrong was acceptable
   The wrong remains wrong. Forgiveness refuses to repeat it.

9. A. Love and peace
   Love and peace are the values practised in this sub-strand.

10. Becoming friends again after a wrong, through apology and forgiveness.
   Peace education in this lesson includes reconciliation.
